title: Arpit Davé on Seizing the Opportunity to Accelerate Science and Deliver Greater Impact for Patients
summary: Learn how BioMarin’s Chief Digital and Information Officer envisions using technology to accelerate innovation for people with rare genetic conditions.
body_markdown:
## **Q: You’ve spoken about being purpose-driven in your career. What experiences shaped your path into biopharma?**


I’ve always been drawn to science and technology. As a student growing up in India, I was fascinated by understanding how complex systems work and solving difficult problems, which is what led me to study engineering and eventually pursue a master’s degree in the United States.


Early in my career, I worked in engineering roles outside of biopharma, but I found myself looking for an opportunity to apply my interests in a way that felt more meaningful. When I entered the industry, I quickly realized I’d found the right fit. What stood out to me was the incredible complexity of the work, as well as the purpose behind what we were doing. In biopharma, we’re bringing together biology, chemistry, data, technology, regulatory processes and healthcare systems to improve people’s health and lives. That puzzle is both intellectually challenging and deeply motivating.


Around that same time, I began forming a belief that has stayed with me throughout my career. So much of what our industry does is built around data, yet there was enormous untapped potential in how that data could be used to generate insights and support decisions. Even when the technology wasn’t quite ready, I could see the possibilities. Over the years, that conviction has only grown stronger. With advances in AI and computing power, many of those possibilities are becoming reality, which makes this an incredibly exciting time.


I continue to be inspired by the purpose of the work, and the challenge of always striving to do it better and faster. The chance to help bring new therapies to people who are waiting for them is what has kept me motivated ever since.
